rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause For Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate covered tenancies without one of the listed at-fault or no-fault just causes, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. It covers most rental units in the City not regulated by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, including single-family dwellings.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and single-family dwellings. Applies once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, some HACLA- or government-owned properties; units covered by the RSO.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease expired; unit not regulated by RSO; excluded facility types (transient hotels, care facilities, cooperatives, owner's roommate, certain government/HACLA properties).

rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) (municipal code section not stated on page)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.conflict_note: Page says the JCO 'can apply to buildings that are newer than October 1, 1978' without specifying whether the cutoff is construction date or certificate of occupancy; effective date and official LAMC citation not given on this page.

rules.title: Eviction for non-payment of rent limited to arrears exceeding Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO and JCO units may not evict a tenant for falling behind in rent unless the tenant owes more than one month's Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Arrears must exceed Fair Market Rent (by bedroom size)
rules.coverage_conditions: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be covered by RSO or JCO.

rules.citation: Los Angeles renter protections (municipal code section not stated on page)
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: All eviction notices served on tenants of JCO and RSO properties in the City must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: File within 3 business days of service
rules.coverage_conditions: All JCO and RSO rental properties in the City of Los Angeles.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be covered by RSO or JCO.

rules.citation: Los Angeles eviction notice filing requirement (municipal code section not stated on page)
rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional change in cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units older than 15 years (rolling) not subject to stricter local rent control such as the LA RSO.
rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years (rolling); deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties with owner occupying the other unit throughout the tenancy; single-family homes/condos not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member where written exemption notice was given; units subject to the City's RSO.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Written notice of exemption given for single-family/condo units; affordability deed restrictions; dormitory status; owner occupancy of two-unit property.

rules.quoted_span: rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.conflict_note: Page describes the 15-year exemption as units 'constructed within the last 15 years'; the statute keys on certificate of occupancy. Effective date inferred from page's rolling-exemption example (January 1, 2020). Page's stated maximum (8.9% for Aug 2024–Jul 2025) is outdated as of query date.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) just cause requirement
rules.requirement: Covered tenancies are subject to state just cause eviction limitations; single-family homes and condos not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member are exempt if the landlord gave written notice.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by AB 1482; in Los Angeles, the local JCO/RSO governs covered units.
rules.exemptions: Single-family homes/condos not owned by a real estate trust, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member where written notice was given (exemption unavailable if more than one dwelling on the lot or a non-separable second unit); other AB 1482 exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Written notice of exemption given to tenant; ownership entity type.

rules.quoted_span: that the tenancy is not subject to the “just cause” and rent increase limitations as specifically described in Civil Code Sections 1946.2(e)(8)(B)(i) and 1947.12(d)(5)(B)(i).
rules.conflict_note: Page only references the state just cause provision in passing via the single-family exemption; details of the state just cause rule are not described on this page.

no_rule_findings.finding: The JCO itself does not regulate rent increases; JCO-only units may be subject to state AB 1482 rent cap instead.
